### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-settings/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**9** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeTursoPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), turso_auth_token (literal, a string literal in contributeKnowledgeTursoSettings), turso_url (literal, a string literal in contributeKnowledgeTursoSettings), /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via action_button (literal, a string literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers; a string literal in specifiers), /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeTursoPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via registerAction (symbol, a method of interface SettingsRegistry))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in knowledgeTursoSettingsSpecifiers))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-settings/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf810f5a4012b69c7c9d1ebf88d0eb768db2195b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d8d827410610fcc36357b3cad7620c2247e46017` — the merge of head `29ed1f480f28045e33c0de6c8441ea81e1178f3b` into base `bf810f5a4012b69c7c9d1ebf88d0eb768db2195b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d8d827410610fcc36357b3cad7620c2247e46017 && git checkout d8d827410610fcc36357b3cad7620c2247e46017
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bf810f5a4012b69c7c9d1ebf88d0eb768db2195b 29ed1f480f28045e33c0de6c8441ea81e1178f3b && git checkout -B drift-repro bf810f5a4012b69c7c9d1ebf88d0eb768db2195b && git merge --no-ff 29ed1f480f28045e33c0de6c8441ea81e1178f3b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf810f5a4012b69c7c9d1ebf88d0eb768db2195b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bf810f5a4012b69c7c9d1ebf88d0eb768db2195b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Local-runs: none

Scope: packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/settings-contribution.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/plugin.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/__tests__/settings-contribution.test.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/__tests__/plugin.test.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-settings-contribution.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/__tests__/knowledge-settings-contribution.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/knowledge.manifest.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/knowledge.manifest.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/knowledge-settings-retired-keys.pin.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-default-action-handlers.pin.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/translations/{ar,de,en,es-ES,fr,ja-JP,ko,pt-BR,ru,zh-CN,zh-Hant}.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts (registerManifest, registerAction, runAction, resetNamespaceRows, the orphaned-secret note), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts (the action door), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-action-copy.ts, packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/plugin.ts outside the hunk (readStoreSettings, resolveStoreUrl, defaultStoreUrl, start, openFromSettings), packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-secret.object.ts and sys-platform-setting.object.ts (apiMethods), .changeset/config.json, AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3), .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/{contract-review,execution-duties,security-findings}.md; the two changesets and content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx are read for ② and for the DELIBERATE CORRECTION.

Inputs read: card #37907 (body, 4 comments, the claim 7217144305 and the dev report 7223647773 included), folded card #37680 (body, 6 comments, the cloud fact 7217205358 and the claim 7217241951 included), PR #37982 (body, 2 comments, 27 files, net diff against the merge base 73d5e347f7), the 54 check-runs on the head, the log of the failed first attempt of Test Core (8/10), and for context the record 7215949880 on PR #37902.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, the narrowing.** `POST /api/settings/knowledge/test` answers `400 SETTINGS_ACTION_FAILED` wherever knowledge-turso does not add its group. RIGHT, and measured rather than asserted: `runAction` finds no handler and returns the no-handler answer, the route maps `ok: false` to that envelope, and three suites pin it against an undeclared control action (`never_declared`) at the HTTP door: the no-store block and the own-url block in knowledge-turso, the retired-keys pin in service-settings, and the mounted-service block in service-knowledge. The base manifest at head declares `chunk_target` alone and no `action_button`.
- **Where the action still answers.** RIGHT. `contributeKnowledgeTursoSettings` registers the manifest with the group, then the handler, in that order (`registerAction` refuses an unregistered namespace; `registerManifest` carries the namespace's earlier handlers, so `rebuild` and `index_status` survive). The store-from-settings block pins the page order `turso, turso_url, turso_auth_token, test` and a 200 where the control is 400.
- **Handler registered only where the group is added.** RIGHT as written: the one `registerAction('knowledge', 'test', ...)` left in the tree outside tests is inside `if (composed !== page)`. service-knowledge registers none; the settings plugin's default map registers none (pin updated). One consequence is S1.
- **Handler body.** RIGHT: moved byte for byte in behaviour (same merge of stored values under the payload, same three answers, same `extractOverrides`). The declared type changed from `SettingsActionHandler` to a local structural pair; it stays assignable (TypeScript Type Check green, and the kernel test registers it on the real service).
- **Boot warning (N2 of the card).** RIGHT in the two cases the card asks for: `init()` warns once when the function answers false under `opensFromSettings()`, and stays silent for a contributed page and for a store with a `url` of its own (four pins). The both-keys return is stricter than before and correct for its purpose. The line's consequence clause is not true in every case it fires; see N2.
- **Public surface.** `@objectstack/service-settings` loses `knowledgeTestActionHandler` (both `src/index.ts` and `src/manifests/index.ts`); `@objectstack/knowledge-turso` gains `knowledgeTestActionHandler`, `KNOWLEDGE_TURSO_TEST_ACTION`, `KnowledgeTursoActionInput`, `KnowledgeTursoActionResult`. No file in the tree at head still imports the removed name from service-settings: `git grep` finds it only in knowledge-turso's source and test, one comment in the default-handlers pin, the two changesets and three CHANGELOG entries. No doc page, skill, example or app names it, and nothing under `packages`, `ui`, `apps` or `examples` calls the door except the button's own declaration.
- **The eleven locale edits, label.** RIGHT. Each service-settings bundle loses exactly the three lines of `settings.knowledge.actions.test` and nothing else; the eleven removed labels equal the eleven added to `knowledgeTursoSettingsTranslations`, string for string. No key is orphaned: the only other `actions.test` in those bundles is the SMS page's.
- **The eleven locale edits, description (#37680).** RIGHT and consistent. The cloud per-organization sentence is gone from the fallback (it was in no locale). Every locale and the fallback lose the "on PostgreSQL ... not read" clause and gain one sentence saying blank uses `knowledge.db` in the data directory; each names PostgreSQL once. The new sentence is true against the code: a blank `turso_url` reads as unset in `readStoreSettings` and `resolveStoreUrl` then opens `defaultStoreUrl`, which is `knowledge.db` in `dataDirectoryOf`. The dropped sentence is false per the cloud fact 7217205358, which this record takes as the card's governing reading and did not re-measure.
- **Manifest version stays 5.** RIGHT: an action button carries an id and no key, and the spec's bump rule speaks of keys.
- **Gate verdicts.** 37 success, 15 skipped, 1 failure, 1 in progress. The failure is `Check Changeset`, judged in ②. The one in progress is `Test Core (8/10)`, judged in ③; this record does not stand in for its conclusion.

### ② Semver level

- **The declaration.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right for the two things the PR body and the dispatch worry about: an export removed from a published entry and a door that now refuses are both narrowings, and neither makes the line a `yes`. Read strictly it under-declares one thing: the criterion is "widens the accept set or enlarges the public surface", the surface is what the built entry reaches, and knowledge-turso's entry reaches four new names. The exact spelling for a diff that does both is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. Nothing downstream differs between the two: both land on the narrowing face at this tier, both are Tier H at the queue guard, and the level is `patch` either way. The record 7215949880 accepted five additive exports under the same spelling on PR #37902. Recorded as N1, the seat's call.
- **Level.** `patch` on `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`, `@objectstack/service-settings` and `@objectstack/service-knowledge`. RIGHT under AGENTS.md: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". All three packages publish a changed source file. A removed export at `patch` is this repository's stated rule, not an oversight; the three packages are in the fixed group at `19.0.0-next.0`.
- **Declared where it must be.** The `!` is in the PR title and the changeset's first line; both declaration lines are line-initial in both carriers and agree; the BREAKING paragraph is there; exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and its reason holds (a settings manifest and its handlers are runtime registrations).
- **FROM/TO.** Present and correct for the two readers it names: the script author is told the answer and to stop calling; the importer is given the one-line import from `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`. "Same check, same answers" is true. A third reader is missing: S1. A smaller omission is N5.
- **Check Changeset red, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** This is the correction class, not a collision: `.changeset/37678-knowledge-turso-settings-group.md` is pending on the merge base, the PR body declares the edit and quotes before and after, and the PR's own note has its own issue-scoped name. One sentence changes, judged clause by clause:
  1. "delete the `knowledge` rows named `turso_url` and `turso_auth_token`, and the `sys_secret` row the `turso_auth_token` row's handle names". TRUE: an encrypted key's row holds a handle in `value_enc` and the ciphertext sits in `sys_secret`.
  2. "without the store no API door clears that key". TRUE on this head: a write naming the key is refused as undeclared; the built-in `reset` walks only the keys the page declares (`resetNamespaceRows` iterates `getNamespace` values); and the data API serves `sys_secret` and `sys_platform_setting` with `get` and `list` only.
  3. "the row is a decryptable copy of the token". TRUE, and it is the settings service's own wording for an orphaned row.
  4. "nothing requires it". TRUE: no reader exists where the store is not mounted.
  The PR body's "no other sentence of that note is made false by this diff" holds under the reading 7215949880 used (a note describes its own step); see N3 for the one sentence that needs that reading. With this record at PASS the correction is confirmed once S1 is closed; the gate stays red by design and no gate is changed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions.** None raised.
- **Deviation: #37680 folded.** Accepted: same file, same group, both claims on the cards, both `Fixes` lines on the PR; the description edits are judged in ①.
- **Deviation: the removed export, taken as ordered.** Accepted. The card says to move the button and its registration into knowledge-turso; the handler body has to follow, because knowledge-turso has no runtime dependency on service-settings and service-settings cannot depend on knowledge-turso without closing a cycle through service-knowledge. A copy left behind in service-settings would be an export nothing registers.
- **Deviation: no backticks around knowledge.db in the twelve strings.** Accepted: the page renders descriptions as plain text.
- **Deviation: the unexpected file `plugin.test.ts`.** Accepted: its settings fake gains the page a real boot has, so the new warning stays silent there; no assertion is loosened.
- **Deviation: draft PR opened before the local run.** Noted; no bearing on this head.
- **out_of_scope: Test Core (8/10).** The first attempt failed on six knowledge-turso cases, each "Test timed out in 5000ms": two in `acceptance.test.ts`, two in `contract.test.ts`, one in `plugin.test.ts` (the `url` option wins), one in `settings-contribution.test.ts` (a URL saved during the boot). The report's sentence that none asserts anything this diff changed needs one qualification: two of the six sit in files this diff edits, and the last runs through the new registration. Neither case's own lines changed, the first takes neither new path (a `url` of its own returns from `init()` early), and the four others are in untouched files; the run shows import 57s and transform 36s for a 65s package run, which reads as runner load. The re-run is in progress at the time of this record. Its conclusion is the gate verdict, not this paragraph.
- **Security.** The action door is gated exactly as before: `runAction` asserts the namespace's write permission before it looks for a handler, so the move changes no permission. This diff puts no secret value into an answer, a remedy or a log line: the handler never returns the token, the new warning names a file path only, and the no-handler answer names the action and namespace. The diff changes no authentication, authorization or secret-handling behaviour, hence the machine line above. One observation about code this diff moves unchanged goes to the seat privately and is not written here; the dev report's security field reads `withheld` and was not available to this review.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).** Nothing to find: no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the settings contract's standing refusal real and takes no delivered capability away. The capability is a form check of two fields. Where the two fields are on the page because their one reader put them there, the check is beside them and answers as before. Where they are not, the check read nothing that deployment reads and opened no connection, and its door now gives the answer every action without a handler gets. That is "delivered where read, retired where not", decided by the party that knows whether it reads the keys, the same shape PR #37902 gave the fields themselves.

Tried to break it:
- Registration order: the handler goes on after the manifest, and the re-registration keeps `rebuild` and `index_status`. Held.
- A settings service without `registerAction`: the function now answers false and adds nothing, and `init()` says so. Within the fixed version group this cannot occur.
- A deployment where the group is contributed but the check is not: none; one branch does both.
- The reverse, a page that carries the fields and a `test` button with no handler: reachable. S1.
- A host page whose own action is named `test`: N4.
- The copy load: `settings.knowledge.actions.test` arrives through the same deep-merging load as the rest of the group; the settings bundle no longer carries the path, pinned in both directions.
- Truth of the warning in each case it fires: N2.

S1 (should-fix) — a host that registers its own `knowledge` page declaring both Turso keys and the `test` button, between the knowledge service's `init()` and this plugin's, now has a dead button with no line saying so. `withKnowledgeTursoSection` returns that page untouched, the handler is registered only inside `if (composed !== page)`, the function answers true (both keys present) so no warning fires, and `POST /api/settings/knowledge/test` answers the no-handler 400. On `main` the knowledge service registered the handler for that page. The pending note of PR #37902 promises this very host that it "keeps that manifest as written", and neither BREAKING bullet of the new note covers it: the first speaks of deployments where the fields are not on the page, the second of importers. No composition in this repository does this, so the reach is a host outside it. Close it on either face: a third BREAKING bullet ("a host whose own `knowledge` page declares the `test` action registers `knowledgeTestActionHandler` from `@objectstack/knowledge-turso` itself"); or register the handler when the page left as written declares the action and both keys, with a pin. The prose route is enough and moves no code.

Nits (none affects correctness or the contract):

N1 — the declaration's strict spelling is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, for the four names knowledge-turso's entry gains (see ②). Same face, same tier, same level. Fix on the PR body and the changeset line, or leave it with the precedent of 7215949880 named.

N2 — the warning's consequence clause ("nothing can be saved there and the store opens its default file") is false in two of the cases it fires for. With no knowledge service mounted the store never opens at all, and `start()` already warns about that separately. With a host page that declares `turso_url` but not `turso_auth_token`, the URL can be saved and the store opens the saved URL. The changeset repeats the clause. The remedy the line gives is right in every case. Accepted deviation or follow-up.

N3 — the pending 37678 note says the plugin "loads the same strings, in the same eleven locales"; after this PR the eleven descriptions differ from the ones that note moved. Both notes ship together and the new one says what changed, so it reads true as that note's own step. Left as is.

N4 — the collision test in `withKnowledgeTursoSection` now includes the generic id `test`. A host page with its own `test` action and no Turso keys gets no Turso fields, where on `main` it got them; the store then cannot be pointed anywhere from the page. It is warned and pinned, and no released version had the fields contributed, so nothing shipped regresses. Accepted deviation.

N5 — the import line sends a service-settings consumer to a package it may not have installed, one whose dependency is a native libSQL client (the entry imports that client as a type only, so the import itself loads nothing native). One clause in the changeset would say so. The two structural types duplicate service-settings' own on a permanent surface.

N6 — the report's account of the six timeouts is slightly too broad (see ③). No action on the tree.

## 席位核对

**Contract review.** Record 7223849938 at this head is PASS at the contract tier (`verify-review-tier` PASS) and carries one graded finding, S1. The queue guard reads S1 as open on this head, so the PR cannot go to the seat until a delta record closes it. I adopt the record.

**What the next head needs.**
- **S1.** A host that registers its own `knowledge` page, declaring both Turso keys and the `test` button, ahead of this plugin's `init()` now has a Test connection button that answers the no-handler 400, and nothing logs that. The smallest fix the record accepts is prose only: a third BREAKING bullet in `.changeset/37907-knowledge-turso-test-connection.md`. It should say that such a host now registers the `knowledge` / `test` handler itself, and give the FROM/TO. If the area would rather close it in code (register the handler for that page too, or warn), it needs a pin case.
- **Optional, nits from the record.** N2: the boot warning's consequence clause is false in two of its four cases, the one with no knowledge service and the one with `turso_url` but no token. Fix it in the same commit if the head moves anyway. N1 to N6 otherwise stand as accepted deviations.

**Rulings on the area's questions.**
- **Declaration.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` stands. The removed `knowledgeTestActionHandler` export and the new 400 are both narrowings. The four names knowledge-turso's entry gains are additive, and record 7215949880 accepted the same spelling on #37902 (N1). `patch` on all three packages is right, and the banner, the `!`, both declaration lines and the ADR-0087 marker are present. No file at this head imports the removed export.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** The rewritten 37678 sentence is true clause by clause against the code (record ②). So the Check Changeset red is the deliberate-correction class, confirmed by an at-tier PASS on the same head.
- **Test Core (8/10).** The re-run is still in progress at this reading. The six 5000ms timeouts are `file:` URL cases. Two of them sit in files this diff edits, but no line of either case changed. Read with the import and transform times, it looks like runner load. The next head needs a green Test Core like any other.
- **Dogfood.** It is owed on the narrowing, and the dev reports the full battery green. It has to be re-pinned on the next head.

**Next:** a new head, then a delta L2 on S1 (and N2 if touched), then a delta L1, then the seat's Tier H handoff.
